name: Golf (Six Card)
description: Six-Card Golf is a matching game where players try to earn the lowest score over nine holes (rounds). Each player manages a six-card layout arranged in a 2x3 grid, replacing high cards with lower ones drawn from the stock or discard pile. The game's unique strategy involves balancing point reduction with the need to match cards in columns to nullify their scores.

history.origins: Derived from the basic four-card version of Golf, the six-card variant became significantly more popular due to the added depth of the 2x3 layout and column-matching rules.
timeline: Mid 20th Century: Variations of Golf evolve from broader rummy/matching families.
1990s: Six-card variant becomes a staple social game in the US and UK.
Modern Era: Digital versions proliferate, often under names like 'Crazy 31' or 'Six Card Golf'.
history.cultural: Popular among social groups and retirees for its balance of luck and simple memory/matching strategy.
history.evolution: The game is part of a large family of 'Golf' games, including Nine-Card Golf and Harakiri.

setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck. For more than 4 players, two decks may be shuffled together.
setup.dealing: Dealer deals 6 cards to each player, face-down, in a 2x3 layout. Remaining cards form the stock. Top card of stock is turned face-up to start the discard pile. Players turn any two of their own cards face-up at the start.

rules.objective: Achieve the lowest total score at the end of nine 'holes' (rounds).
rules.gameplay:
1. Players take turns clockwise.
2. ACTION: Draw the top card from the stock OR the top card from the discard pile.
3. REPLACEMENT: Use the drawn card to replace any one of your six cards (face-up or face-down). The replaced card is discarded face-up.
4. DISCARDING: If drawing from the stock, you may choose to discard the card immediately instead of using it to replace, but you must then turn one of your face-down cards face-up.
5. ENDING: When a player has all cards face-up, everyone else gets one final turn. Then scores are tallied.
keyRules: You cannot look at your face-down cards before choosing which one to replace.
A pair of equal rank in the same column scores 0 points for that column (e.g., two Queens in one column = 0).
Kings are the most valuable cards to hold as they score 0 individually.
The hand ends when one player's cards are all face-up; they 'knock' (figuratively) and other players play once more.

strategy.basic: Prioritize replacing high cards (10s, Face cards) immediately. Try to match ranks in columns to erase even high numbers.
strategy.intermediate: If you draw a high card from the stock that matches a face-down card you suspect is there (or just for a chance), replace a face-down card to keep the match option open.
strategy.advanced: Watch your opponents' layouts. If they have many face-up cards, the round will end soon; prioritize flipping your own face-down cards to avoid being caught with unknown penalties.
tips: Kings are worth 0 - keep them even if they don't match.
Always try to pair 2s or Aces to get a 0-point column.
If you are ahead, keep flipping cards to end the round faster.

variations.name: Nine-Card Golf
variations.description: Played with a 3x3 grid (9 cards). Column matching only works for three-of-a-kind.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant uses different grid size and column rules; engine overrides can be added when implementing the variant.

variations.name: Harakiri
variations.description: A variant where 'Knocking' carries a penalty if the knocker doesn't have the lowest score.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Knock penalty rule differs; overrides can be added when implementing this variant.

scoring.description: Players tally their card values at the end of each round. Rounds continue for nine 'holes'.
scoring.winCondition: Lowest total score after 9 rounds wins.

synthesis.shortDescription: A strategic matching game where players juggle a 2x3 layout, aiming for column pairs and face-card removal to achieve the lowest total score.

hero.title: SIX-CARD GOLF
hero.subtitle: Mind the Grid
hero.tagline: Swap, pair, and flip. Hit the lowest score in nine holes.
